Me after 4 minutes in game: "Man, this is... weird. Easy, but also fun." Me after 22 minutes in game: "Oh, so THAT's how they get you... interesting. Wait, wtf is that block!? I don't trust it." Me after 45 minutes in game: "HAHAHAHA, MINIGUN GO BRRRRRRRR!" My wife after I am 88 minutes in the game: "So... Am I assuming correctly that you're not gonna do much more than this?" Which is code for: "You're definitely NOT gonna keep playing!" That being said, I thought I was playing for ~30 minutes. This game is odd, but in a good way, as in "it sticks out" from all the mushy "formula-X for maximum profit" games that we all know too well. It's like Wall-World, Vampire Survivors and Minecraft hat a really bad, drunken night and now try to figure out who the parents are, because even tho the child certainly LOOKS like all three, it doesn't really take after any of them. It's relatively simple, but it gets challenging after a few maps. The biomes offer a change in scenery and how the scenery tries to get back at you. The temporary upgrades allow for super fun combinations and altogether, I didn't expect a game like this to be so entertaining. It also manages fairly well to feel claustrophobic, which I never thought is gonna be a thing in 2D game. So yeah... flying steampunk dwarves, going full auto vs. goblins and other underground dwellers. If Warhammer had a lighthearted steampunk setting featuring dwarves, this probably would be it. Also: Aiming is for elves! As of now, I love it and I'd say go for it. This is balm form my ADHD brain, just like Vampire Survivors. Edit: Dude, my soundbox must be full of stones, because the music I am getting from this is rockin'.

I finished all achievements including 100%. But I still have some disappointing parts. At first there were stories, quests, upgrades, a lot more then I expected. But after progressing about 50% of the map, there's nothing more to do in the game. And I've got disappointed in 3 parts. First, there were no place to spend gold after upgrading everything. I know other games like this also have no place to spend gold other than upgrades, but the problem was that upgrades were finished before even progressing 50%. This was disappointing because, the fun of going around the map is to get more gold. But when the upgrades were over, I lost my purpose of going around the map and started pressing 'only the down arrow' until I reached the bottom. There should be somewhere else to spend gold, or at least the upgrades should be more expensive so that the upgrading gets finished at the later part of the game. Second disappointing part was that nothing happened at 100% of the progression. So the last 40% of the game was pretty same to me, because I just pressed the 'down arrow' till I reached the bottom. I got bored from doing that, but I still played the game to see the ending. I thought there would be a last fight, a story, or at least an ending credit, but nothing happened... Last disappointing part was that there's no reroll in the game. If there was a reroll, I could have tried making drone build or explosion build, close combat build or etc and this would have gave me more fun. Even if it's not that, I could've evaded the situations like picking one of the 3 skills that I don't want. But It's still worth the money for me,

I really WANT to recommend this game. The gameplay loop fantastic, the sound is fun, and it has a lot of 16-bit era attitude that hits just right. And I've got a minor love for games that center around dwarves including DRG & Dwarf Fortress. However, I've had it for 40 minutes or so, and it has thrown every window on my system into geometric chaos and crashed my GPU drivers 3 times -- each time I get too involved in a jungle/poison gas biome. I've updated to the latest Catalyst drivers, and it's still no good. So let me just say this. I'm not refunding it. It's earned enough goodwill even despite that, so I'm giving it another 2-3 months to see if the developers figure out the bug and fix it, and I'll hopefully come back and see if my recommendation changes. But for now, it's still not ready for full release. Edit: Well, it's been two months, and the game still crashes in the jungle biomes. Really a shame. I wanted to play this game, but I can't. Edit 2: Revisited the game 2 years later (on Linux now), and it seems to no longer crash. Can't tell you if the original bug was fixed due to the OS change nor how long it took to be fixed, so I'm not changing the recommendation.

Oh boy another "I wish Steam had a better system than Yes/No" review. But that's just it. It's fine, plays fine, nostalgic of really really good flash games from the mid 2000s when flash games were really really good. There is nothing wrong with this videogame. The reason for my negative review is, after a certain amount of meta upgrades the game is just so extremely easy to the point of tedium. I'm not exactly looking for a hard game, but all the upgrades and systems and mechanics start to feel like they'd better suit a game with steeper requirements for a win condition. If you've played, seen, or heard of Galactic Mining Corp, this is basically that with a little bit of Vampire Survivors bolted on, which is, again, just good game design. Only Galactic Mining Corp manages to keep ahead of you with its gradually increasing difficulty, where this game falls behind you and never quite catches back up. The last 4 hours of my gameplay have been: select level, beat level, do that again. There's a lot of levels and very few of them mix up the formula or present enough of a challenge that I'd need to change my tactics. I like the game, I am not bothered that I bought the game, I would literally buy a Mahjong game if it had a Space Dwarf Mining theme attached to it. But apart from a sheer number of levels and a barebones story, there's not a lot here. But it's cheap, and it's space dwarves, so, I still bought it and I'd still buy it again lol.

It's Sunday after a week of staying home after a bad cold. Yesterday I was finally well again and went to the bar and compensated for a missed week. Something I'm paying for today. My friend sent me a suggestion to play this game and since I wasn't really in the mood for anything involving any kind of brain activity this seemed like a match. Breezing through the first few encounters and then my first death occurs - by the lack of fuel. A resource I really wasn't paying attention to. I think one of the pixly dwarf faces said something about it but I accidentally skipped through that dialogue. Oh well. Doesn't seem to be any penalty at all for dying anyway, so let's bore on. A couple more locations in and an alarming sound starts blaring. It stops, then comes back. I fly around, trying to see if there's some special enemy? A special block? Then I realize it's the song 'Hard Core' by Urban Thermo Dynamics that fooled me. My own fault for always turning off game music. Most temporary upgrades (the ones that only last for the current level) are quite underwhelming. At least until you unlock the third pilot. But even then the rate of fire upgrade is a sure bet. More often than not I have to choose between the least worst. Constantly wishing there was an upgrade that showed you where the closest fuel block was rather than the unending flood of upgrades that help you diminish foes. Foes that rarely pose any threat since you're hardly ever killed by them. It's still the fuel (which by the way acts as a timer for how long you can explore a location before finding the exit). But the fuel problem disappears a bit into the game. But talking of enemies, that crawling large goblin is the weirdest one I've seen in a while. I can't decide if that's a bad or a good thing. I pause a couple of times and look at it, scratching my head. It took 2 hours until I noticed my character had a surname. A while after that I decide to change character. Not because I want to but just because of deciding to write a review. And I regret not switching earlier. The description "homing missiles" made me think they were mainly targeting enemies. That is not the case. And when you unlock further dwarves there's never, ever, any reason to go back to the previous one. I should also add that there's no huge difference in play style between them at all. The game is really, really, repetitive and quite purposeless. This feeling is further enhanced by being too easy. The challenge curve goes from "no challenge at all" to "I can turn on auto-fire and play this blindfolded". Some other minor inconveniences: Accidentally entering a location - can't escape out of character selection you have to play the level (or enter the level and exit). You can't see which temporary upgrades you've already chosen when picking a new one. If you run out of fuel you can't refill by shooting a fuel block while falling. Enemies are nuisances. And only that. Not once did I feel an accomplishment of diminishing them. Not even the boss which only hit me once because I started looking at something else than the screen during the boring battle. I don't really understand the point of having such a large over world when there's not that many differences between the locations. Every text prompt, where the story is unfolded, interrupts your shooting so you have to repress the mouse button to continue shooting. Something that irks me more and more due to my Sunday state. But since there is no real reason ever to not empty your guns all over I think there should be a toggle button for us lazy individuals. And when I write this I realize I didn't check. ♥♥♥♥. There it is!

[h1][b]向下直挖三千里[/b][/h1] [h1]前言[/h1] 《深地爆破采掘》是一款机制简单却又有着爽快玩法的像素风Rogue游戏。 玩家将要驾驶一架采掘直升机，一路深入地下，摧毁一切挡在眼前的障碍，最后寻得宝物。 [h1]挖穿地心[/h1] 本作的玩法很简单，只需要像《钻地小子》、《铲子骑士：挖掘》、《Mining Mechs》那样一路向下探索即可。 玩家驾驶的采掘工具是一架直升机，其可以向前发射无限子弹来摧毁各类地形，获取资源的同时为自己打开前路。 地形方面，除了可轻易开采的泥土外，还有难以被击毁的岩石、冰原、丛林等地形，这些地形的价值较低，而各种较鲜艳的方块则代表了可被开采并收集的高价值矿石。 此外，还有一些特殊方块，如可获取大量资源的宝箱、摧毁后能炸开一片空间的炸药、开采后可补充燃料的矿石等，这些内容构成了游戏的基本游玩体验。 向下探索一定距离或是完成指定任务后，界面中会出现终点箭头，跟随前往便会找到巨型宝箱，里面一般存放着永久解锁项目。 [h1]横冲直撞[/h1] 本作中有三项重要的数值，分别是技能、升级以及燃料。 [list][*]- 技能：随时间充能，发动之后能提供短时间的爆发能力，此时可以驾驶飞机直接撞击并摧毁前方的一切方块。 [*]- 升级：随收集到的资源充能，完成之后可以进行一次三选一构筑。 [*]- 燃料：随飞行缓慢减少，燃料耗尽将会导致飞机坠落。[/list] 其中技能虽然持续时间短，但是冷却充能时间也很快，一次探险过程中就能提供多次爽快的横冲直撞体验。 燃料则限制了玩家无限开采发育，和飞机的耐久度以及敌人配合，为游戏增添了不少挑战性。 [h1]构筑之美[/h1] 接下来便是本作的局外升级和局内构筑项目了。 局外升级较为简单，基本是一些数值的提升，如提高伤害、射速、射程、飞行时间、增加拾取矿石的范围、降低技能冷却时间等。 局内构筑便是玩家之前在各个地图收集到的内容，这些构筑项目大幅提升了游戏体验，如加强攻速、攻击力、将子弹变为小幅爆炸弹，甚至是增加一支枪管向后射击。 也有一些构筑能为游戏带来多种玩法，如每隔一段时间自动向下释放的钻头，其可以钻出一条深深的隧道，配合爆炸模块，就可以直接在下方炸出一个深坑，直接将游戏变成了简单模式。 [h1]结语[/h1] 《深地爆破采掘》是一部小品级别的Rogue游戏，用简单的玩法延伸出了爽快的游戏体验。 伴随火爆的Bgm一路向下开采，横冲直撞深入地心，这个过程非常解压。 [quote] 妙笔提手点墨花，妙语成章满纸纱。 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44852326/]猪式会社[/url]，用心绘测游戏。[/quote]

I thought I would enjoy this game, and it had a positive score, but I was quite disappointed. I like digging games, but I didn't find digging fun in this one and I think it's because it doesn't feel meaningful, you're pretty much just going to want to go straight down unless there's quest items, and then left or right where the end is. There's no reason to explore, because everything only gives more of the same currency, and fuel will run out if you do. It gets very repetitive very fast. The enemy swarms can get intense later, but they're not challenging in an interesting way, they just come at you from different directions, and I found them annoying more than interesting to try to contour and defeat. The second character is at least more interesting to play I found, because it creates more room to fight the enemies in, but it still wasn't enough to make it a fun time. And the temporary upgrades could be more interesting or exciting. If you enjoy just blasting through rocks and shooting enemies that come around you then you might enjoy this one, but I think it would need to change a lot to be worthwhile, at least from my own impression of it.

First five hours of gameplay are extremely satisfying, you feel getting more and more powerful as the maps get bigger and bigger, some events happen in some maps, the risk/reward balance is well done, and above all : like in any good game with meta progression you pile up more and more money to spend it in the upgrade shop. And then all of this satisfying escalation crumbles down. Money gets useless since evreything is maxed out, in a game where mining for money is the core mechanic it's a bit contradictory. Everything is unlocked. You finish any map easily, no more event except some basic object collection missions. And yet the game continues without any challenge or cool thing to do. Play this game for the satisfying early game but beware : the endgame is boring.

Bore Blasters isn't a bad game but it becomes repetitive and tedious long before you are close to getting through the plot. Somewhere around 50-60% completion you stop unlocking new things and just get temporary buffs, and the buyable upgrades aren't very meaningful at that stage either. Each level feels the same as the last since there isn't much build variety

Sideways Thumb. The core gameplay loop is solid. Mining blocks feels good, the helicopter feels responsive, and the hurtboxes are generous. Played in short bursts (a couple of levels) is optimal. However, the pacing slows down a ton at around 60% completion (around the same time as the last two upgrade tiers for all of your stats) at which point not even the most elegant of proc gen levels can help the game not feel repetitive. A lot of the run upgrades are either too similar (an unknown amount of fire rate/damage increase) or "not impactful enough" (the drones never felt strong no matter how many times I upgraded any of them) but the novelty of finding out about all of the upgrades lasted long enough to get me to that 60% completion mark where most of the game's auxiliary systems start to break down. I feel like the game is trying to toe the line between "casual mining simulator" and "baby's first bullet hell" and that experience feels as "mixed-bag" as it sounds if you were like me and looking for more of the latter. The story is fine and kept me engaged up until this point but because of the way the map is structured (almost a 10x10 grid where you can play any level adjacent to one you've cleared) the story snippets can get duplicated/out of order if you don't go radially outward from the starting point (which basically defeats the point of letting the player choose what levels to do). Performance wise, the more cpu-intensive builds (EX: explosions triggering projectiles with bouncy bullets) cause the frame rate to drop substantially on my gtx1080 (as low as 20fps down from 120fps) for the last third of the longer levels. I doubt they're efficiently managing off screen particles, but with that many particle effects on screen, maybe someone would think the frame drop is charming and not the mark of an inexperienced dev team. Good luck to them in their next games. Def get this on a sale if it looks good, the game is exactly what it looks like in the trailers but unfortunately was not really for me.

Very satisfying game from start to ... half. At first you upgrade your ship and weapons, you unlock new biomes and new types of enemies and stuff. Everything is very enjoyable and feels great to play. The action is great. Although it can tank your fps if you have hundreds of particles blowing around ^^. The whole gameplay loop is good. At least for the first 6-8 hours until you experience everything this game has to offer. And then you are left with like half of the game left to explore that has barely any objectives (you get some quest very sporadically, every 3-4 levels or so). Most of quests are very simple - dig where the arrow shows and collect an item or several of them. That's it. Every level ends once you reach a chest at the very bottom of a level. And for the last 8 hours you are left to do just that - jump into a level, dig straight down for several minutes and complete the level, rinse and repeat. Even the chest is basically at the same spot 90% of the time. There is no fun to be found. It's like the game has all the content in the first half and the second half is just templates of levels that you somehow need to get through to 100% the game. I think the easiest solution would be just to delete like 40% of all levels (or to add content to them so that every single dig has something more to offer than the repeating gameplay loop). Quality of experience over quantity should be the goal. Right now this game overstays its welcome for 8 out of 16 hours.

In the vast minefield of roguelites and arcade shooters, BORE BLASTERS blasts its way into the spotlight with a quirky concept and pixel-perfect execution. Developed by indie studio 8BitSkull, this game is equal parts mining, mayhem, and mechanical mastery. At its core, BORE BLASTERS is a frantic, twin-stick shooter where you pilot a heavily armed drill-copter straight down into the earth. Your mission? Carve your way through layers of rock, harvest precious gems, and survive waves of underground threats. It’s a fast-paced loop that perfectly balances chaos and control. Each run is procedurally generated and only lasts a few minutes—short enough to keep things snappy, but packed with tension. The deeper you go, the tougher the enemies and terrain, forcing you to adapt on the fly with quick upgrades and split-second decisions. Visually, the game’s retro pixel art shines. Environments are colorful, destructible, and delightfully animated. Enemy designs are varied, from angry mole-bots to lava-dwelling horrors, all backed by a punchy synth soundtrack that keeps your adrenaline spiking. Sound effects are crisp and satisfying. Each gem ping and explosion lands with weight, giving you constant feedback without overwhelming the action. Between runs, you’ll use collected gems to upgrade your gyrocopter with stronger weapons, faster drills, and cooler abilities. This meta-progression keeps the game feeling fresh even after dozens of dives. Still, the progression can feel grindy after a while. With no overarching narrative or campaign, motivation depends entirely on your love for the core loop—which, fortunately, is extremely fun. BORE BLASTERS doesn’t pretend to be more than it is—and that’s its strength. It’s a pick-up-and-play adrenaline rush with bite-sized runs, clever enemy design, and just enough upgrade depth to keep you coming back. If you enjoy roguelites, drilling mechanics, or twin-stick chaos, this one’s a gem. Pros: -Addictive arcade gameplay loop -Crisp, charming pixel visuals -Short, high-intensity runs perfect for quick sessions -Satisfying upgrades and unlocks Cons: -Can feel repetitive in long bursts -Light on story and world-building Rating: 8/10

Bore Blasters is a digging / mining / roguelite game in which you shoot blocks, venture deep down into the ground, hunt for gems, and complete small missions. You then upgrade your ship with your found gold to complete more difficult missions. There are 3 characters to play as and each have his / her own style of play with strengths and weeknesses. The game took just over 20 hours to complete 100%. + The gameplay (mostly) never got stale in my 20 hours of playing. Shooting blocks and trying out various strategies to complete missions was always fun. There are many different weapon combos that when used together can make for ultimate destruction. + The writing and banter of the dwarves / goblins was always entertaining. + Very addicting. + Great soundtrack / music. + The game is long. + Fun boss fights - The later missions of the game, I would say hours 18-20 near the end, can feel a bit repetitive. - Could have used a few more boss fights and enemy variety. - Could have used more of a variety of missions objectives. Excellent game for lovers of digging / mining games. Overall: 8.5/10
